lesson.title: Nine Months of Change: The Three Stages of Prenatal Development
lesson.summary: Prenatal development unfolds in three distinct stages, from a single fertilized cell to a fully formed newborn, and it shows how biology and environment start shaping a person before birth even happens.
lesson.body:
Development does not begin at birth. From conception to birth, roughly 38 weeks, a single fertilized cell becomes a newborn with billions of interconnected neurons, and psychologists divide this process into three stages: the germinal, embryonic, and fetal periods.

The germinal stage covers roughly the first two weeks after conception. The fertilized egg, now called a zygote, divides rapidly as it travels down the fallopian tube, and around ten to fourteen days after conception it implants in the uterine wall. If the developing cell mass splits in two during this period, identical twins result.

The embryonic stage runs from about the second through the eighth week. This is when the major body structures and organ systems form: the neural tube that will become the brain and spinal cord closes, the heart begins to beat, and limb buds appear. Because so many organs are being built for the first time during this window, the embryonic stage is generally the period of greatest vulnerability to disruption, a point that matters a great deal for the next chapter on teratogens.

The fetal stage runs from about the ninth week until birth. The structures laid down earlier now grow and mature: bones harden, muscles strengthen, and organs become functional rather than just present. Movement usually becomes noticeable to the mother sometime in the second trimester, and the brain undergoes especially rapid growth in the final months, which is part of why babies born very early often need significant medical support.

Even before birth, nature and nurture are already intertwined. Genetic instructions guide the basic plan of development, but the prenatal environment, including maternal nutrition, stress, and exposure to outside substances, can shape how that plan unfolds. That interaction is exactly what the next chapter explores in more detail.
